Hon'ble Ravi Nath Tilhari,J.
Heard Sri Radhey Shyam Dwivedi, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned standing counsel for the respondent nos. 1, 3 and 4 and Sri Kaushalendra Nath Singh, learned counsel appearing for the respondent no. 2.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioners with the following prayers :
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to protect the petitioners from eviction by the respondents from their site of squatting/vending as per the mandate of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 as well as notification dated 15.06.2017 of the Chief Secretary for implementation of Section 3(3) of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

(iv) Issue any other writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case.
(v) Award the cost of the writ petition in favour of the petitioners."

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the issue involved in this writ petition was subject matter of another writ petition namely Writ C No. 28417 of 2019 which was finally disposed of by another co-ordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 17.09.2019 and hence this writ petition may also be disposed of on the same terms and conditions subject to which the aforesaid writ petition was decided.
Learned standing counsel does not dispute the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners.
The judgment and order dated 17.09.2019 passed by another co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Writ C No. 28417 of 2019 is being reproduced hereinbelow :
"1. Heard Sri Michael Peter, learned counsel for petitioners, learned Standing Counsel for respondents 1, 3 and 4 and Sri Kaushlendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for respondent 2.

sentences.text: (b) Set aside the Press Release dated 25.07.2019 of respondent no.2, which is against the mandate of the provisions of the act and the Rules thereunder along with the Government orders mentioned (supra) and the orders passed by this Hon'ble High Court mentioned (supra) along with several other orders passed since 2014.

(c) Direct the respondents not to dispossess or evict or disturb the petitioners from their site of vending at Sector-58-59, Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh till the certificate or license is granted to the petitioners as per Section 3 of The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

3. Case set up by petitioners is that fundamental rights guaranteed to petitioners under Article 14 and 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution for doing business is being violated by respondent authorities by removing street vending shops from their respective sites at Sector 58-59 of Noida and not allowing them to continue their business.
They are being harassed by authorities/ respondents abrupting their livelihood and some times they are not allowed to squat and vend at their site.

Petitioners'
business is in no way hindrance to either smooth pedestrian movements or obstruction to pavement or parking.

Petitioners are dealing in night markets in the area where Call centres of various MNCs,
Media Houses and various other business centres which are operating at night catering to the international market and country, providing the call centres, business centres and items related thereto to all the employees at night, without any disturbance to any public and pedestrian movement as well as vehicular movement.
Petitioners i.e vendors and squatters in order to have legally vending business

have complied with various Rules and Regulations in terms of Food Licenses for Food Safety and Health Standards as mandated by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "FSSAI"), Section 26-C of Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1973") and carrying on their business without any encroachment.

sentences.text: Photographs of sites are also placed on record.

It is said that protecting rights of street vendors, various orders have been passed from time to time but ignoring all these orders and also provisions under "The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014" (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 2014") and rules framed thereunder i.e.
"The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Rules, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as "Rules, 2017")

sentences.text: " respondent 3 has issued a press release for removal of petitioners' street vending stalls/shops etc., which is patently illegal.

4. Learned counsel for petitioners placed before us various orders of this Court as well as Act, 2014 and in particular Section 3 of Act, 2014 which provides for survey of street vendors and protection from eviction or relocation till completion of Survey and allotment of alternative site.
He contended that unless a survey of street vendors is conducted by Town Vending Committee, petitioners cannot be removed.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for respondent 2 submitted that petitioners have encroached upon public land causing obstruction in free flow of traffic and, therefore, authorities have issued notices to petitioners directing them to vacate the site or they shall be removed.
6.
We have heard argument of counsel for respective parties and perused Act, 2014, Rules, 2017 and entire relevant record.

7. Act, 2014 was enacted considering significant contribution made by 'street vendors' to urban society as a whole, more specifically to the comparatively poorer sections, and to enable them to earn a livelihood through creation of good working conditions, without causing obstructions to the public as well as securing rights of citizens to have adequate means of livelihood as enshrined in Articles 14, 19 (1) (g), 38 (2), 39 (a), 39 (b) and 41 of Constitution of India and fostering a congenial environment for urban street vendors to carry out their activities, without harassment from any quarter and a mechanism for regulation of street vending activities.
Act, 2014 contemplates different kind of 'Vendors' namely 'mobile vendors', 'stationary vendors' and 'street vendors'.

Section 3 of Act,
2014 reads as under :-
"3. Survey of street vendors and protection from eviction or relocation.-(1) The Town Vending Committee shall, within such period and in such manner as may be specified in the scheme, conduct a survey of all existing street vendors, within the area under its jurisdiction, and subsequent survey shall be carried out at least once in every five years.
(2) The Town Vending Committee shall ensure that all existing street vendors,
identified in the survey, are accommodated in the vending zones subject to a norm conforming to two and half per cent of the population of the ward or zone or town or city, as the case may be, in accordance with the plan for street vending and the holding capacity of the vending zones.
(3) No street vendor shall be evicted or, as the case may be, relocated till the survey specified under sub-section (1) has been completed and the certificate of vending is issued to all street vendors."
8. Section 4 of Act, 2014 provides for issue of certificate of vending and reads as under :-
"4. Issue of certificate of vending.-(1) Every street vendor, identified under the survey carried out under sub-section (1) of Section 3, who has completed the age of fourteen years or such age as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government, shall be issued a certificate of vending by the Town Vending Committee, subject to such terms and conditions and within the period specified in the scheme including the restrictions specified in the plan for street vending:
Provided that a person, whether or not included under the survey under sub-section (1) of Section 3, who has been issued a certificate of vending before the Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168793707/
4 commencement of this Act, whether known as licence or any other form of permission (whether as a stationary vendor or a mobile vendor or under any other category) shall be deemed to be a street vendor for that category for the period for which he has been issued such certificate of vending.

sentences.text:
( 2) Where, in the intervening period between two surveys, any person seeks to vend,
the Town Vending Committee may grant a certificate of vending to such person,
subject to the scheme, the plan for street vending and the holding capacity of the vending zones.

(3) Where the number of street vendors identified under sub-section (1) or the number of persons seeking to vend under sub-section (2) are more than the holding capacity of the vending zone and exceeds the number of persons to be accommodated in that vending zone, the Town Vending Committee shall carry out a draw of lots for issuing the certificate of vending for that vending zone and the remaining persons shall be accommodated in any adjoining vending zone to avoid relocation."
9. Section 14 of Act, 2014 provides duty of street vendors and reads as under :-
"14. Duty of street vendors.-Where a street vendor occupies space on a time sharing basis, he shall remove his goods and wares every day at the end of the time sharing period allowed to him."
10. Sections 15 and 16 of Act, 2014 deal with maintenance of cleanliness and public hygiene and maintenance of civic amenities in vending zone in good condition respectively and read as under :-
"15. Maintenance of cleanliness and public hygiene.-Every street vendor shall maintain cleanliness and public hygiene in the vending zones and the adjoining areas."
"16. Maintenance of civic amenities in vending zone in good condition.-Every street vendor shall maintain civic amenities and public property in the vending zone in good condition and not damage or destroy or cause any damage or destruction to the same."
11.

Supreme Court has also considered rights of 'Street Vendor' and in Maharashtra Ekta Hawkers Union and Ors. Vs. Municipal Corporation, Greater Mumbai and Ors. , 2004 (1) SCC 625 has said as under :-
"The above authorities made it clear that the hawkers have a right under Article 19 (1)
(g) of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Maharashtra Ekta Hawkers Union and Ors. Vs. Municipal Corporation, Greater Mumbai and Ors. , 2004 (1) SCC 625
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This right, however, is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19 (6).

Thus, hawking may not be permitted where e.g. due to narrowness of road, free flow of traffic or movement of pedestrians is hindered or where for security reasons an area is required to be kept free or near Hospitals, places Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 27 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168793707/
5 of worship etc.

entities.text: Raj Kumari And 39 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no fundamental right under Article 21 to carry on any hawking business.
There is also no right to do the hawking at any particular place.

The authorities also recognize the fact that if properly regulated, the small traders can considerably add to the convenience and comfort of the general public by making available ordinary articles of every day use for a comparatively lesser price.
The scheme must keep in mind the above principles..................."
(emphasis added)

12. Thus, Supreme Court has clearly said that right of street vendors subject to reasonable restrictions in the light of fact that public convenience namely movement of public on road,
pavement etc, is not obstructed.
13. Learned counsel for petitioners submitted that in para 15 of this petition, he has stated that petitioners are making no encroachment or obstruction in smooth running of commuters/metro riders.

14. However, we find that this is a disputed question of fact, since, respondents are proceeding to remove petitioners from the sites on the ground that they have encroached upon the same causing hindrance to smooth pedestrian movements or obstructions to pavement or parking.
This is also evident from photographs placed on record by learned counsel for petitioners showing that either pavement has been occupied or roads have been encroached upon.
15. In these circumstances, in our view matter requires to be considered by concerned authority at the first instance.

16. In view thereof, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, we dispose of this writ petition permitting petitioners to approach concerned authority by moving appropriate representation, and in case, such a representation is made, Respondent-Authority shall investigate into the fact whether petitioners are doing their business of Street Vendors without encroachment on public land and without obstructing free flow of traffic etc.

and if these facts are found correct,
only then the competent authority of respondents shall consider their cases in the light of provisions of Act, 2014 and Rules framed thereunder and pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within two months from the date of receipt of representation along with a certified copy of this order.
17. With aforesaid observations, this writ petition is disposed of."
It is not disputed amongst the learned counsel for the parties that the controversy involved in this writ petition stands concluded by the aforesaid judgment.

In view of the above, this writ petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioners to file a representation before the concerned authority and in case any such representation is made, concerned authority shall investigate into the fact whether petitioners are doing their business of Street Vendors without encroachment on public land and without obstructing free flow of traffic etc.
